yzu-ty_station.scenic: The path along the creek behind YZU is quieter and has more trees. It’s a nicer walk than staying on the main road.
yzu-ty_station.alerts: Be cautious around the big intersection near the Zhongli–Taoyuan border. Cars turn quickly and scooters often roll through crosswalks.
yzu-ty_station.tips: If biking, use the bike lane on Chunri Road—it’s smoother and avoids most of the heavy traffic heading toward the station.

ty_station-ty_night_market.scenic: Walking through the small alley streets gives a more local feel and is shaded during the day.
ty_station-ty_night_market.alerts: The sidewalks near the night market become extremely crowded after 6pm. Walk slowly and watch out for scooters weaving through the crowds.
ty_station-ty_night_market.tips: Transit is often faster at peak hours—take a short bus ride if you're carrying shopping bags or tired from the station walk.

yzu-ty_night_market.scenic: Take the side roads near Hutoushan for a quieter walk with trees and small parks along the way.
yzu-ty_night_market.alerts: The uphill section near Hutoushan can be dark at night with limited street lighting—avoid walking alone late.
yzu-ty_night_market.tips: Combine biking + walking: bike most of the way, then park before entering the night market area since cycling isn’t allowed inside.
